reaction_equations: Al-containing molecules + As-stabilized surface -> Al atoms incorporated into Al sites + alkylradicals terminate Al-stabilized surface
alkyl radicals desorb from surface during hydrogen purge
surface_mechanism_description: The self-limiting growth mechanism involves the adsorption of Al-containing molecules onto the As-stabilized surface, incorporation of Al atoms into Al sites, termination of the Al-stabilized surface by alkylradicals, desorption of alkyl radicals during hydrogen purge, and reaction of Al atoms with AsH3 to form AlAs.
evidence: At first, for the ALE-AlAs growth, the decomposed Al-containing molecules start to adsorb onto the As-stabilized surface (Fig. 1a). Al atoms are incorporated into the Al sites of AlAs, and alkylradicals that are connected to the Al atoms then terminate the Al-stabilized surface. Once the alkylradical-terminated Al surface is formed, further adsorption of Al-containing materials does not occur. Growth proceeds until the surface is fully covered by Al atoms with alkyl radicals. In the next hydrogen purge step (Fig. 1b), alkyl radicals start to desorb from the surface, and a bare Al metal surface appears. Next, sufficient AsH3 gas is supplied to the surface (Fig. 1c), and this gas reacts with Al atoms to form AlAs. Finally, hydrogen is purged to completely remove extra As atoms (Fig. 1d).
